content:
Buy at Rs. 1,200, sell at Rs. 1,500 — profit 25%, not 20%. Why? Because profit per cent always stands on the COST price. That single sentence sorts out most of this chapter. The free IMO Class 7 Profit and Loss online test below has 10 exam-pattern MCQs with instant scoring. Treat it as a diagnostic. Every explanation tells you what to revise.

What the IMO asks from Profit and Loss in Class 7

  • Profit, loss and their percentages (on cost price).
  • Finding SP from CP with profit/loss %, and the reverse.
  • Discount on marked price.
  • Simple interest: SI = P × R × T / 100.
  • Finding principal, rate or time from SI.

Key facts and formulas to revise first

  • Profit % = profit/CP × 100 — the denominator is ALWAYS cost price.
  • SP = CP × (100 + profit%)/100 in one step.
  • At 15% loss, SP of a Rs. 1,400 cycle is 1400 × 0.85 = Rs. 1,190.
  • SI is the same every year — interest of Rs. 240 over 2 years means Rs. 120 per year.

Mistakes that cost Olympiad marks

  • Computing profit % on the selling price.
  • Treating discount % as profit % (discount stands on MARKED price).
  • Using months directly as T in the SI formula (convert to years).

quiz.title: IMO Class 7 Profit and Loss Quiz
quiz.intro: Ten Olympiad-pattern questions. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.
quiz.about: IMO Maths Olympiad Class 7: Profit and Loss

questions.q: A man buys a cycle for Rs. 1,400 and sells it at a loss of 15%. The selling price is:
The cost price of 10 chairs equals the selling price of 5 chairs. The profit percent is:
questions.explanation: SP of 5 chairs = CP of 10 chairs, so SP of 1 chair = 2 × CP. Profit = CP, i.e. 100%.

questions.q: A man sells two articles for Rs. 4,000 each, gaining 20% on one and losing 20% on the other. His net result is:
questions.explanation: Equal SPs with equal gain and loss % always give a LOSS of (x/10)²%. Here (20/10)² = 4% loss.

questions.q: An article marked at Rs. 8,000 is sold at a 15% discount. The selling price is:
A shopkeeper marks goods 30% above cost and allows a 10% discount. His profit percent is:
A marked price of Rs. 5,000 gets successive discounts of 20% and 20%. The selling price is:
A merchant marks up 10% and uses a 900 g weight for 1 kg. His total gain percent is about:
questions.explanation: Charges 1.1 × 1000 = Rs. 1,100 (cost of 1 g = Re. 1) for goods costing Rs. 900. Profit = 200/900 ≈ 22.22%.

questions.q: The simple interest on Rs. 5,000 for 3 years at 8% per annum is:
Rs. 23,500 is invested at 10.5% per annum for 3 years. The simple interest is:
An article sold at 20% profit would, if bought 10% cheaper and sold Rs. 15 cheaper, give 25% profit. Its cost price is:
questions.explanation: New CP = 0.9x, new SP = 1.2x − 15. For 25% gain: 1.2x − 15 = 1.125x. 0.075x = 15 gives x = Rs. 200.
